The last time I played this franchise was WWE 2K24 during another Free Weekend last year.

Honestly, I prefer 2K24 over 2K25, mainly because 2K24 offers a solid gameplay and great story about John Cena. It gives an insight into his highs and lows, the glory and bitterness behind being a WWE star. I'm not a fan but after around 3 hours of gameplay, I was able to experience some of his most important and extraordinary matches, and I learned that he's a genuinely nice and respectable person.

In 2K25 I didn’t find a story mode. The Showcase focuses on introducing famous fighters and families, but those are individual matches rather than full stories.

The gameplay feels similar to 2K24, though it takes longer to trigger special moves. 2K25 isn’t bad, but I prefer the previous game.

WWE 2K25 is an incredible wrestling game with a lot to offer. The gameplay is solid, and the variety of modes ensures there's something for everyone. That said, it’s disappointing that the Island feature isn't available in the PC version—it's a fun addition that would’ve made the game even better. Despite that, the game still shines with its smooth mechanics, deep customization options, and engaging gameplay. If you're a wrestling fan, this is definitely worth playing!

This is a great game and I do intend on keeping it. HOWEVER, The Island not being on PC should be criminal! This whole thing of excluding PC Gamers from things because of hackers is crazy. Especially when PC is the measuring mark for a games success. It's simple, Invest more into the security of your game. Especially if it's full of micro transactions in the first place!

It's good, but wait for a sale if you're on PC. I paid $125 on PC for basically no online content.

In my opinion.. this is just WWE 2K24, slightly improved with better visuals.

PROS: 
- My GM mode is better than before! adding an acutal online / co-op ordeal to this was such a great move!
- Universe mode has gotten a great overhaul and is a lot easier to work with! 
- Entrances / free cam during entrances looks amazing!

CONS:
- My Rise is just... so dull.. and doesn't feel ANYthing like how a wrestling story mode should. Its unbareable.
- NO ISLAND FOR PC PLAYERS? Dope! I spent $130, to not play a feature that was advertised heavily to begin with because "PC won't be able to handle this" Right... 
- Lack of online matches / player v player matches. 
- My faction is just mid, and is the only remotely decent thing allowing players to fight one another.

Overall... 5.5/10

WWE 2K25 is the wrestling game equivalent of a Vince McMahon court case — long, painful, and nobody really wins. For £60, you get a buggy mess that crashes more than WWE’s legal team during deposition. The game’s glitches pile up like backstage secrets, and the AI acts like it’s dodging subpoenas — completely unpredictable and ready to ruin your night. MyRise mode is about as satisfying as waiting for Vince to admit fault, and Universe mode books itself into a corner faster than Owen Hart fell through that cage. Matches freeze, characters vanish, and commentary repeats like a broken promo loop. Playing this game feels like you’re stuck in an endless contract negotiation — except you’re the one paying. If you want an actual wrestling experience, skip the drama here and watch old PPVs. WWE 2K25? It’s a tragedy in every sense

Coming from WWE 2K22 and WWE 2K24, this game is without a doubt the strongest entry. The improvement from WWE 2K22 to 2K24 was massive, but they actually hit it out of the park with this one. The AI, character variety, gameplay tweaks, the different match types, and the different fighting styles that now actually really make the wrestlers feel different (i.e., powerhouses, technicians, strikers, etc.) feel very unique; also, animation-wise, it just makes this game feel amazing. 

After the sh*tshow 2K26 apparently is when it comes to their battle pass model where you have to unlock tons of characters you already paid for via DLCs, which can take tens of hours; WWE 2K25 might be the last and best entry in the franchise worth buying for quite some time to come.

PS: With modding tools it is very easy to unlock all the DLC characters you own in the game, so if you don't want to do any of the grinds, that will save you time. To my awareness, this is not yet working with 2K26, so there is that.

WWE 2K25 is a solid step forward — great graphics, smoother gameplay, and fun modes that keep you coming back. It’s easily one of the better modern 2K entries.

That said, the older WWE games like SmackDown vs. Raw still hit different. They had a charm and depth that today’s games haven’t fully recaptured yet.

My only real complaint: stop adding the same wrestler multiple times. Just give us one superstar with all their personas, gears, and versions in one clean slot. Having them separated feels outdated and honestly a bit unnecessary.

Overall though, still a good time for WWE fans.

This was my first time buying a WWE game in over a decade. I first started playing since Smackdown Vs. Raw THQ days. 2K definitely changed things up but saw their negative habit of implementing microtransactions which i also agree is too much. With that being... WWE 2K25 was extremely fun to play. Great entrance graphics, in-ring battles, background music, etc. But I came across numerous bugs such as crashing my PC at startup. It would suddenly freeze the entire operation of my PC during the trademark loading screen. I have a 4070 Ti Super with a Ryzen 7 7700X. I can well over handle the PC specs considering others are playing at even older card generations. I have been searching over threads and people are also coming across issues of PC crashing. This game was not meant to be played on PC considering 2K has already removed the new 'Island' which is exclusive for consoles. That being said. Although i enjoyed playing with only 4 hours in, the constant crashing of my PC and having to restart, and re-validate my files was not worth my time. I will most likely only start buying WWE on console. OR if this game was not so expensive to begin with all of the bugs currently going on... I'd consider repurchasing when the crashes have been resolved.

The ai is only set to target the player and even when they basically have nothing left in the tank, somehow the ai will counter EVERYTHING the player does. The constant need to do everything in 3s is annoying too, i.e. closing ambulance doors gets easier after the 3rd time, submissions miraculously become more effective after the 3 time, takes 3 sig/finish for 3rd pin attempt to stick, etc. I can beat the life out of an opponent and even after 3-bars of finishers, a signature, they have no health, their health bar body is red and their actual body is visibly beat up, but I still have treat it as if the match just started because the first 3 attempts to end the match will be thwarted by the games "rule of 3s". Let's not forget, the way women's matches are setup, a lot of the content won't be played because I HATE FORCED TRIPLE-THREAT/FATAL FOUR-WAY MATCHES! The best part of the game isn't the wrestling, it's the amount of stuff that can be created and shared. I have the most fun creating things to upload rather than wrestling in matches, solely because they think we all want FFW/TT matches.

tldr.text: Mixed (67%): players praise the story, characters and gameplay, while bugs and crashes are the main complaint.
Recent reviews are more positive at 81%, but that is based on far fewer reviews.

details.text: Players who have just started are far less positive than players in the middle of the playtime range, who sit at 74%.
For someone buying now, bugs and crashes are the main risk, with 19% of reviews raising them and one saying the game "crashes constantly".
